::: {#def-positional-invariance .theorem}
## Positional invariance

A component function $g_{ti}$ is positionally invariant with respect to [network graph](#def-graph) $\mathscr G_t$ if it (a) depends only on the network values $\mathbf X_{\mathcal N_i}$, and (b) is unchanged by a permutation of those values together with the same permutation of the network weights: for all $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{X}' \in \{0,1\}^n$ and every permutation matrix $\mathbf M$,

$$
\mathbf{X}_{\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\mathbf{X}'_{\mathcal{N}_j}, \quad \boldsymbol\Psi_{i,\mathcal{N}_i} = \mathbf{M}\boldsymbol\Psi_{j,\mathcal{N}_j} \Rightarrow g_{ti}(\mathbf{X}) = g_{tj}(\mathbf{X}'),
$$

where $\boldsymbol\Psi_{i,\mathcal N_i}$ is $\boldsymbol\Psi_i$ restricted to the neighborhood of $i$.

An exposure mapping is positionally invariant with respect to a graph set $\mathcal H = \{\mathscr{G}_t\}_{t \in [1:T]}$ if it is [separable](#def-separability) and each component function is positionally invariant with respect to an element of $\mathcal H$.
:::
